CAA.intro: Certification Authority Authorization records name the certificate authorities allowed to issue certificates for this domain. An authority left out has to refuse, which limits the damage a mistake or a compromise can cause.

issue.title: TLS certificates
issue.help: The certificates securing HTTPS, and any other TLS service of this domain and its subdomains.

issuewild.title: Wildcard TLS certificates
issuewild.help: A single certificate covering every subdomain at once, such as *.example.com.

issuemail.title: S/MIME certificates
issuemail.help: Used to sign and encrypt e-mails sent from an address of this domain.

issuevmc.title: Verified Mark certificates (VMC)
issuevmc.help: Used to display your verified logo next to your messages in mailboxes.

explain.any: Any certificate authority may issue {{kind}} for this domain. This is what happens when nothing is published, and it is the widest setting.
explain.restricted: Only the authorities listed below may issue {{kind}} for this domain. Any other one has to refuse.
explain.none: No authority may issue {{kind}} for this domain. Choose this when you know you never use them.
explain.inherit: Wildcard certificates follow the rule chosen for TLS certificates above. Set a rule here only if they deserve a stricter one.

CAA.pick-one: No authority chosen yet: as long as this list stays empty, any of them may issue.
CAA.incident-response-text: Where should a certificate authority report an attempt to violate this policy?
CAA.contact-info-text: Published so a certificate authority can reach you about your certificates. It authorizes nothing by itself.

CAAPolicy.name: Certification Authority Authorization
CAAPolicy.description: Indicate to certificate authorities whether they are authorized to issue digital certificates for a particular domain name.
